items.item_text: 01. Have you completed college-level coursework in facility management, business administration, industrial engineering, supervision, or a related field? If yes, please attach a copy of your transcripts or degree verifying the related coursework upon submission of this application. Options: Yes | No
02. Do you have a valid California Class C driver's license? If yes, please attach a copy of your valid driver's license upon submission of this application. Options: Yes | No
Facility permit management, civic center usage procedures, and event logistical coordination.
Conduct thorough site quality audits and verify client compliance with facility permit agreements.
Valid California Class C driver's license and maintain insurability under District vehicle insurance coverage.
Bureau of Security and Investigative Services (BSIS) training or certification preferred.
Certified Playground Safety Inspector (CPSI) or Qualified Applicator Certificate (QAC) highly desirable.
Plans, schedules, assigns, supervises, and evaluates the work of custodial, grounds, and facility support staff assigned to evening, weekend, and holiday shifts.
Conducts regular site inspections and quality assurance audits across District schools to ensure cleanliness, building security, grounds maintenance, and adherence to established standards.
Assists in prioritizing, scheduling, and assigning routine and urgent work orders; ensures appropriate tools, equipment, and cleaning supplies are available for evening crews.
Supervises facilities operations for facility permits, community usage, athletic events, and district evening functions; coordinates setup, staffing, and teardown.

Meets with permit holders and community clients; inspects facilities immediately following events to verify district obligations were met, calculate damage/equipment fees, and reconcile expense estimates.
Monitors security systems, access controls, and radio communications; serves on the emergency response rotation to resolve after-hours intrusion alarms, weather disruptions, or facility emergencies.
Ensures assigned evening and weekend staff receive mandatory safety education, personal protective equipment (PPE), hazard communication training, and comply with Cal/OSHA standards.
Oversees the implementation of night, weekend, and holiday setback programs for building systems, HVAC, and lighting to reduce District energy consumption.

Establishes performance standards, conducts formal evaluations, counsels employees, and prepares supporting documentation for recognition or progressive discipline in accordance with Merit System rules and labor contracts.
Participates on employee selection panels, conducts unit staff meetings, manages payroll/timekeeping records, and processes initial-level formal and informal grievances.
Principles and practices of effective shift supervision, workload scheduling, and staff development.
Plan, organize, schedule, supervise, and evaluate the work of evening, night, and weekend operational personnel across multiple District sites.
Methods, materials, chemical safety (M.S.D.S./SDS), tools, and modern equipment used in building custodial, grounds maintenance, and facilities operations.
Exercise sound independent judgment and administrative discretion in resolving after-hours operational conflicts, security alarms, and emergencies.
District Merit System rules, human resources policies, and collective bargaining agreement provisions governing classified personnel.
Apply labor contracts and Merit System rules constructively in managing performance, grievances, and shift assignments.
Applicable federal, state, and local safety regulations, including Cal/OSHA, fire codes, and building security protocols.
Maintain flexible work hours, including evenings, nights, weekends, holidays, and on-call emergency response duty.
Energy management setback procedures and automated building system operations.
Communicate clearly and effectively, both orally and in writing, with site administrators, staff, vendors, and community groups.
Be flexible to perform work within changing priorities and possess sufficient interpersonal skills to work harmoniously with staff, students, administrators, parents, community members and others.
